# Greek Drills

> Free web tool for practicing Ancient Greek paradigms (morphology): parse a form, choose the right form from four close alternatives, or type it. Works in any browser, no account. https://greekdrills.ijfen.com/

## What it drills

- Verbs: thematic verbs in the present, imperfect, future and root (second) aorist, in every mood, with infinitives and participles; deponents; εἰμί
- Nouns: first, second and third declension (Mollin's types 1, 2 and 3), including irregular nouns such as ἀνήρ, γυνή, Ζεύς
- Pronouns: the article; personal pronouns and αὐτός; reflexive, demonstrative, relative, interrogative and indefinite pronouns
- Adjectives: first- and second-declension (2-1-2 and two-ending 2-2) adjectives

## Features

- Three drills: Parse (identify tense, voice, mood, person, number, case, gender), Choose (multiple choice with near-miss distractors), Type (answer in polytonic Greek or Latin letters using Beta Code; accents optional)
- Questions can be asked with grammar terms or with context, e.g. τῆς [καλός] ψυχῆς
- Practice by Textbook: one tap sets up a drill for everything taught up to a given chapter of Mollin & Williamson (An Introduction to Ancient Greek), Athenaze, Hansen & Quinn (Greek: An Intensive Course), Mastronarde (Introduction to Attic Greek), or Reading Greek (JACT)
